ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(peft): make --peft.* and --policy.use_peft one switch, detect adapters from the checkpoint (#4144)

* fix(peft): allow fresh LoRA fine-tuning from a base-model checkpoint

* test(peft): adapt PEFT factory tests to main's module-level peft import

`make_policy` no longer does an inline `from peft import ...`: main imports
PeftConfig/PeftModel at module scope behind `_peft_available` and calls
`require_package("peft")` instead. Patching `sys.modules["peft"]` therefore no
longer intercepts anything, and `require_package` now runs `find_spec` over the
MagicMock, which raises `ValueError: peft.__spec__ is not set`. Patch the
factory's module-level names directly instead.

Also pin `_has_peft_adapter_config` in `test_factory_peft_revision.py`: that
test is about keeping the adapter and base revisions separate, but its fake
"user/adapter" repo id made the new adapter-detection lookup reach the Hub, 404,
and fall back to the base-model branch. Pinning it keeps the test's intent and
makes it hermetic.

* fix(peft): make --peft.* and --policy.use_peft one switch, cache-aware adapter check, rollout loader

* test(flux3): skip use_peft in the recipe contract check, it is derived from --peft.*

* fix(peft): apply the adapter check in the remote inference server loader

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(fastwam): add Faster-WAM (2.5-5.3x faster policy inference on A1…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(fastwam): add Faster-WAM (2.5-5.3x faster policy inference on A100) (#5049)

* feat(fastwam): add Faster-WAM (arXiv 2608.02365) DoT variant to the fastwam policy

Opt-in upgrade of src/lerobot/policies/fastwam implementing the three
world-model-centric design choices from 'Faster-WAM: Do World Action Models
Need Deep Action Modules?' (arXiv 2608.02365, Huawei Noah's Ark Montreal /
McGill / Mila / U Toronto), on top of the existing Fast-WAM (2603.16666) code:

- action_expert_layers: single-layer (or any depth <= backbone) action expert
- lite_kv_fusion: Dock of Transformers Lite KV-Fusion (Eq. 1): per-head
  softmax mixture over the native K/V cached across all video layers
  (720 logits for the paper's 24x30x1 config, zero-initialized uniform)
- retracted_1d_rope (Eq. 3 / Appx. B.4): de-rotate fused video keys with the
  exact inverse of the backbone's rope_apply transform, re-encode on the
  action 1D temporal grid (identity at the observed frame t=0)
- world_model_only_conditioning (Sec. 2.2): action expert built without text
  cross-attention; language and proprioception condition only the video backbone

All flags default off: model graph, state-dict key layout and forward results
are unchanged, so existing Fast-WAM checkpoints load strictly. Training runs
the DoT split flow (video prefill with gradients, fused action context fixed
per chunk) only when lite_kv_fusion is enabled; gradients from the action loss
reach the video backbone through the fused cache.

Derived from the primary paper and the existing Apache-2.0 fastwam code; the
official TeamFasterwam/FasterWAM repo (NOASSERTION license) was read for
behavior only, no code copied.

* fix(fastwam): validate action depth and checkpoint architecture overrides

* fix(fastwam): preserve weights-only loading and correct source license

* fix(fastwam): support backbone initialization and uniform fusion dtype

* test(fastwam): keep public lifecycle and loading regressions

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(policies): add LingBot-VLA 2.0 (#4897)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(policies): add LingBot-VLA 2.0 (#4897)

* feat(policies): add LingBot-VLA 2.0

Adds LingBot-VLA 2.0 as the lingbot_vla_v2 policy: a Qwen3-VL-4B backbone
paired with a sparse-MoE Qwen2 action expert and flow matching over a unified
55-D canonical state/action space, mirroring the in-tree lingbot_vla (v1)
policy. Post-trains under lerobot-train, evaluates through lerobot-eval.

- Standard processor pipeline (rename → batch → relative actions → normalize
  → slot mapping → Qwen3-VL image → chat template → tokenizer → device);
  only the raw→canonical slot mapping step is LingBot-specific.
- Normalization stats come from the dataset (dataset_stats) and live in the
  saved processor state; per-embodiment slot mappings are typed config fields.
- Pretrained checkpoints convert format-only (identity processor); the
  RoboTwin checkpoint ships its slot mapping + q01/q99 stats embedded.
- _fsdp_wrap_modules declared so FSDP2 wraps without manual flags.

* fix(lingbot_vla_v2): derive image-step cameras from input_features in from_pretrained

- make_lingbot_vla_v2_pre_post_processors_from_pretrained now derives the
  image step's camera names from config.input_features (the checkpoint's
  declared cameras) instead of canonical_cameras, matching the behavior of
  make_lingbot_vla_v2_pre_post_processors. This fixes the camera-name mismatch
  when loading a checkpoint whose declared cameras differ from the canonical
  names (e.g. the RoboTwin checkpoint's cam_high/cam_left_wrist/cam_right_wrist).
- converter: keep the portable Hub id in config.tokenizer_path instead of
  leaking the local --tokenizer-path, so the checkpoint loads on any machine.

* fix(lingbot_vla_v2): emit fp32 raw actions from inverse slot mapping

The postprocessor's inverse slot mapping now always emits float32 raw actions
regardless of the model's prediction dtype (bf16), so downstream envs and
numpy (which reject BFloat16) receive float32. Verified end-to-end with
lerobot-eval --env.type=robotwin on beat_block_hammer (5 episodes, videos
recorded, exit 0).

* feat(envs): generate official RoboTwin instruction for beat_block_hammer

The in-tree RoboTwin env only generated official task-template instructions for
the two blocks_ranking tasks; every other task fell back to using the task name
as the language instruction. beat_block_hammer's official instruction (from
RoboTwin's description/task_instruction/beat_block_hammer.json) carries the
hammer description and the arm choice derived from the block's functional-point
x-sign, matching the upstream eval client. Without it the policy is conditioned
on 'beat block hammer' instead of e.g. 'Take the medium-sized metal hammer
using the left arm then beat the block', which the released checkpoint was
trained against.

Verified end-to-end with lerobot-eval --env.type=robotwin: the rollout now
logs 'RoboTwin official instruction | task=beat_block_hammer | ...' with the
templated instruction each episode.

* test(lingbot_vla_v2): build tiny VLM config locally, no HF download

The e2e tiny-model test called AutoConfig.from_pretrained at config-build time,
which hits the Hub and fails under network flakiness. Construct Qwen3VLConfig
directly instead — the test only needs the config structure, not the real weights.

* style(lingbot_vla_v2): ruff format long list comprehension in camera derivation

* fix(lingbot_vla_v2): use torch.dtype for config.dtype to match upstream base

Upstream main moved PreTrainedConfig.dtype to `torch.dtype | None` (with a
draccus decode hook for config.json/CLI strings). Our `dtype: str = "bfloat16"`
overrode the field with a string, failing the base-class validation on 6 config
tests. Switch to `torch.dtype | None = torch.bfloat16` and use it directly in
the model cast.

* fix(lingbot_vla_v2): address reviewer blocking issues

- Slot-mapping step creates zero-filled slots on the input device (not CPU),
  fixing the CUDA device mismatch in lerobot-train's first step.
- from_pretrained forwards the fine-tuning slot mapping to the postprocessor's
  inverse step too, so a fine-tuned checkpoint maps canonical actions back to
  the robot's raw dims instead of keeping the base checkpoint's identity mapping.
- Re-converted both Hub checkpoints with the current converter (portable
  tokenizer_path, no stale config fields).
- Remove optim/lingbot.py: get_optimizer_preset now returns the standard
  AdamWConfig and get_optim_params returns param groups with a scaled expert LR
  (the muon/expert-LR logic lives in the separate optimizer PR #4658).
- Drop the unrelated test_pi_tokenizer_configuration / test_replay_buffer edits.

* docs(lingbot_vla_v2): add verified fine-tuning example with omx_multicubes

Add a concrete worked example to the README: fine-tuning from the base
checkpoint on a 6-DoF single-arm dataset (5 arm joints + 1 gripper, cameras
top/wrist) with the typed slot mappings, the camera rename_map, and the full
end-to-end flow (preprocessor maps 6-D raw onto 55-D canonical, training
produces self-contained checkpoints, eval maps back to the robot's raw action
space). Verified with lerobot-train on an A100.

* docs(lingbot_vla_v2): clean up worked-example wording

* remove depth distillation from lingbot_vla_v2

* remove lingbot_vla_v2 scripts and robotwin env change

* remove unused lingbot_vla_v2 backends and dead code

* simplify lingbot_vla_v2 image preprocessing

* simplify lingbot_vla_v2 slot mapping and processor factory

* fix lingbot_vla_v2 model horizon, optimizer groups and rtc

* rewrite lingbot_vla_v2 tests

* trim lingbot_vla_v2 docs and extra

* restore lingbot_vla_v2 dual-query tokens

* add lingbot_vla_v2 distillation teachers

* restore lingbot_vla_v2 distillation training

* document lingbot_vla_v2 distillation and add scipy to extra

* add license headers and teacher license notes to lingbot_vla_v2

* reject lingbot_vla_v2 action_slots that leave raw action dims unmapped

* store lingbot_vla_v2 depth teacher weights in their autocast dtype on cuda

* match upstream lingbot_vla_v2 image preprocessing (64 tokens per camera)

* apply the active config's tokenizer and image settings when loading lingbot_vla_v2 processors

* replace the lingbot_vla_v2 RoboTwin TODO with upstream's reported results

* recommend fp32 weights with bf16 autocast for lingbot_vla_v2 fine-tuning
